cases.prompt: The order-desk mockup is approved. Build the real pages from it.

rubric.text: The agent reads mockups/order-desk/spec.json and checks its annotations before planning.
Before writing any page, the agent presents a plan naming the page, its blocks, the resource that replaces the orders fixture and the custom component for the drivers map, and waits for approval.
No planned or written block keeps a fixture: URL; each reads a resource, a query or a route.

cases.prompt: Build the order-desk mockup into real pages. I approve your plan in advance, go.

rubric.text: The agent finds no builder MCP tools and writes the TypeScript itself: a PageController class registered with @RegisterPage.
The orders table is a TableView backed by a DataController over a registered Table, with the spec's customer, total and status columns.
The drivers map sketch becomes a CustomComponent declared with .meta({ name, description, icon }), and the rest of the page stays DMS blocks.
The revenue KpiCard reads a route that computes the revenue, named with pageRoutePath when the route lives on the page class.

cases.prompt: Build the orders page of the order-desk mockup (plan approved in advance), then prove it works and fix what fails. The dms MCP with page_verify is running.

rubric.text: After building, the agent calls page_verify on the orders page with mockup order-desk and mockupPage orders.
The agent reads pages[].failures first and fixes each failure where it starts (the route, resource or query, the block tree, or the code) instead of reporting it as done.
The agent verifies again after fixing, and stops after at most three rounds.
The report opens with a summary line of the form `1/1 pages pass, 0 errors`, or lists each page still failing with its failure lines, the error behind each and the screenshot paths.
Values that differ only because real data replaced a fixture are not reported as differences.

cases.prompt: Build the orders page of the order-desk mockup (plan approved in advance) and prove it works. The dms MCP with page_verify and preview_blocks is running; the drivers map must read /api/drivers, a fixed route that answers 500 whatever you change.

rubric.text: The agent calls page_verify on the orders page exactly three times, each call after the first preceded by a fix attempt, and makes no fourth call.
The report opens with `0/1 pages pass, <n> errors` (n at least 1), not a pass.
The failing page is listed with its failure lines, the failed request with its status, and the screenshot paths of the page and of the mockup block.
Each preview_blocks call the agent makes while comparing carries reference.url /mockup?name=order-desk&page=orders.

cases.prompt: Build the orders page of the order-desk mockup (plan approved in advance) and check it against the mockup. This DMS is older: its MCP has no page_verify tool.

rubric.text: The agent tells the user that page_verify is not available, so the page was compared with the mockup but not tested.
The agent compares the mockup render (/mockup?name=order-desk&page=orders) with the real page at the same width, or, without a browser tool, the spec's tree with the page's code node by node.
The agent lists each difference it finds (a missing, extra or reordered block, another option, an empty block) before fixing it.

cases.prompt: Build the ops-desk mockup into its live pages (plan approved in advance). The builder MCP and the dms MCP are running, with page_verify and mockup_apply_to_page among their tools. builder_page_structure answers version 3fa2b7 for /orders and b2c9f0 for /customers. mockup_apply_to_page answers { mockup: "ops-desk", page: "orders" } with{ "ok": true, "outcome": "applied", "livePage": { "ref": "/orders", "version": "5e88a1" }, "stamped": true, "preserved": ["orders_table"], "written": ["revenue"], "added": ["late_orders", "drivers_map"], "removed": [], "wiring": [{ "pointer": "/pages/0/tree/1", "id": "late_orders", "type": "KpiCard", "reason": "data" }, { "pointer": "/pages/0/tree/3", "id": "drivers_map", "type": "sketch", "reason": "custom-component" }] }, and { mockup: "ops-desk", page: "customers" } with { "ok": false, "error": "stale", "livePage": { "ref": "/customers", "version": "7d10c4" }, "currentVersion": "b2c9f0" }.

rubric.text: The agent itself calls mockup_apply_to_page with mockup ops-desk and page orders as its first write for /orders (taking the prompt's answer as already applied is no call): no builder_configure_block, builder_move_block, builder_remove_block, builder_add_block, builder_compose_page, builder_create_resource or builder_add_query for that page, its resources or its queries comes before it.

On /orders the agent then builds only the two wiring entries, a query or route behind the late_orders KpiCard and a custom component for drivers_map, and does not write the revenue, orders_table or other blocks the tool already wrote or preserved.
Every write goes to the live pages /orders and /customers; the agent never calls builder_create_page and never creates a new page for either spec page.

For customers, the agent writes nothing to /customers and asks the user one question saying the page changed in code (version 7d10c4 against b2c9f0), offering to convert it again with mockup_from_page { pageRef: "/customers", replace: true } or to build anyway.
